q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal ?

I. It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.

II. NGT is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

III. NGT has six places of sitting throughout the country.
explanation: I is correct (NGT Act 2010). II is wrong: the NGT is not bound by the CPC 1908 and follows natural justice. III is wrong: the NGT sits at five places (Principal Bench New Delhi and zonal benches at Pune, Bhopal, Chennai and Kolkata), not six.

notes.text: - **Full form:** **National Green Tribunal**; created by the **NGT Act 2010** – a **statutory (not constitutional)** body; constitutional anchor **Article 21** (right to a healthy environment), not Article 28.

- **Procedure:** **not bound by the CPC 1908** (or the Evidence Act); follows **natural justice**; powers of a civil court; applies sustainable development, precautionary and **polluter-pays** principles and **absolute liability** for accidents.
- **Five places of sitting** (New Delhi + 4 zonal) – not six; zonal bench is at **Pune, not Mumbai**; Jodhpur and Shillong are only **circuit** benches.

q:
In the context of distinctions existing between a Public Bill and a Private Bill, select the statement/statements that is/are valid:

I. A Private Bill which has been introduced by a Member of Parliament sitting in the opposition and which has been approved by the House will have to be referred to the law department for consultation.

II. A Public Bill is always introduced in the Parliament by the Minister or a member of the government party.

III. A Private Bill will not reflect the policy of the government but upon its approval by the House, a Private Bill would have reflected the policy of the government.

IV. Public Bills and Private Bills, regardless of the differences between them, are governed by the same general procedure, and are required to be passed through the same stages in the House.
explanation: Only IV: both Bills follow the same procedure and stages. I is wrong (a private Bill is drafted by the member, not referred to the law department); II is wrong (a public Bill is introduced only by a minister); III is wrong (a private Bill does not become government policy).

notes.text: - **Article 117** = "special provisions as to Financial Bills"; Art. 117(1): no Bill **imposing a tax** can be introduced except on the **President's recommendation**, and not in the RS. An amendment **reducing or abolishing** a tax needs no recommendation.

q:
Assertion (A): Andhra region was not greatly affected by the Revolt of 1857 as Andhra had no local leaders.
Reason (R): The then reigning Nizam, Nawab Afzal-ud-Dowla adopted a pro-British attitude.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
explanation:
Some keys (and the old app notes): both true, R not the explanation, reading A as 'Andhra was little affected'. Strictly the reason given in A is false, so A as stated is false (NextGen modern level 3 part 1 p.41, p.43).
A is false: Andhra did have local leaders in 1857 – Korukonda Subba Reddy, Dandasena and Sheikh Peer Saheb – and it was little affected because most people stayed loyal and valued the Company's stable rule. R is true: Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula stayed loyal and ordered the conspirators arrested.

- **Andhra did have local leaders** (Subba Reddy, Dandasena, Peer Saheb), so "Andhra was little affected **because it had no local leaders**" is **false** (APPSC G2 Mains 2025 A/R: **A false, R true**).

explanation: Terrigenous deposits come from land and lie mainly on the shelves (I); muds are their finest material (III) and mud colour depends on chemical content (IV). They become finer, not coarser, away from the shore, so II is wrong: I, III and IV.

q:
Arrange the following temples of Ellora in chronological order according to their time of construction :

I. Ravan ki Khai

II. Kailasanatha

III. Dashavatara

IV. Dumar Lena
explanation:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (IV, I, III, II); it is added as option 5.
Dhumar (Dumar) Lena, Cave 29, is one of the earliest Ellora excavations (6th century, Kalachuri period). Ravan ki Khai (Cave 14) was begun before the Dashavatara (Cave 15, with Dantidurga's inscription of c. 753–57), and the Kailasa (Cave 16, Krishna I) came last. So the order is IV, I, III, II, which no printed option gives. The printed key (III, I, IV, II) is wrong on two counts: it puts the Dashavatara before Ravan ki Khai and Dumar Lena third.

notes.text: - **⚠ Settled:** none of the printed options gives this order; the printed key "III, I, IV, II" puts the Dashavatara before Ravan ki Khai and Dumar Lena third – both wrong (Caves 14 and 15 were begun before 16; Cave 29 is Kalachuri-period).
- **Order (G1 2023):** **Dumar Lena (29) → Ravan ki Khai (14) → Dashavatara (15) → Kailasa (16)** = IV, I, III, II.
